key_insight: Block diffusion offers a quality–efficiency trade-off for longitudinal EHR modelling, with one configuration delivering approximately 1.43× faster evaluation than autoregressive modelling.
clinical_relevance: More efficient EHR modelling could support clinical prediction research, but these findings do not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Compared block-based masked diffusion with autoregressive modelling on MIMIC-IV.
Matched tokenisation, context length, model capacity, and evaluation conditions.
Varied block sizes and decoding strategies; assessed generative rollout and frozen linear probes.
evidence_signal: The B=8 configuration achieved approximately 1.43× faster evaluation, while frozen linear probes showed near-identical prediction performance across diffusion and autoregressive representations.
watch_item: Generative rollout generally underperformed autoregressive modelling, and larger denoising budgets produced diminishing returns.
paper_title: Block Diffusion for Longitudinal EHR: Accuracy, Efficiency, and Representation Trade-offs
